item.title: Sony has confirmed that the recently released PS5 firmware 14.23 update is required before playing GTA 6, in a social media post boosted by Rockstar Games.
item.description:
Sony has confirmed that the recently released PS5 firmware 14.23 update is required to play GTA 6, in a social media post boosted by Rockstar Games.
Yesterday November 17, Sony released PS5 system software update 26.07-14.23.00, which weighed in at 1.267 GB. According to Sony’s official patch notes, it makes “some security fixes to the system software.”
Now, just hours before GTA 6 launches at midnight across the world, the PlayStation Support U.S. X / Twitter account confirmed what many had suspected: “Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI. Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they’re ready to play on launch day, November 19.” The official Rockstar Games account then reposted it to its 23.7 million followers.
GTA 6 Dynamic Weather Screenshots
Why has Sony issued this PS5 update warning?
It is believed this unprecedented PS5 update cuts PlayStation Network access to older firmware, which means if you haven’t upgraded to 14.23 you will not be able to play GTA 6 on PS5. 14.23 released just a day after a prominent PS5 hacker claimed to be the first person to have “dumped” a game binary at 14.22, although they did not share any jailbreak.
The PlayStation homebrew scene has made headlines in the last two months for releasing PS5 jailbreaks for prior firmwares. For example, late September, a jailbreak that supported all PS5 consoles running firmware 7.00-13.60 sent shockwaves through the homebrew community because, at the time, it meant that all PS5s, including the PS5 Pro, that hadn't been updated within the previous week were compatible with the jailbreak. This was of huge significance for Sony and the security of the PS5, as people with a jailbroken PS5 can modify their console, potentially opening the door to video game piracy.
However, it was found that some PS5 games subsequently required the more recent 14.00 firmware in order to download updates, sparking a renewed effort to release a new jailbreak for the updated system software. So, there is a game of Whac-A-Mole at play where the homebrew scene is working to release a new jailbreak for the latest PS5 firmware, then do it all over again when Sony releases a new firmware update designed to beef up security.
This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak was made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC.
The question for Sony is whether it can do enough to eventually win this game of Whac-A-Mole with the homebrew scene. This is something of an existential crisis for Sony, which publishers and developers rely upon for the security of their PlayStation releases. But with the emergence of powerful AI models, the stakes have risen significantly.
Just last week, Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, told IGN that the company was taking security seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version.
During an investor-focused Q&A, Zelnick was asked multiple times about this AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up.
“This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations.
“That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.”
GTA 6 is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, and some companies have even given staff bonus time off to play it. We've got plenty more on GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 launch, including details on the New Zealand trick people are using to play early, Gangland Tales From the Frontline of Rockstar's Real-Life Grand Theft Auto Research, and — finally — confirmation of the actress who plays Lucia.

item.title: The Grand Major, an official tournament for Embark Studios' first-person shooter The Finals, is at the center of a heated debate after the developer replaced its real-life esports casters with AI commentators in a now-deleted highlight reel.
item.description:
The Grand Major, an official tournament for Embark Studios' first-person shooter The Finals, is at the center of a heated debate after the developer replaced its real-life esports casters with AI commentators in a now-deleted highlight reel.
Embark Studios is facing backlash after a now-deleted video was uploaded to The Finals' official social media accounts recapping highlights from The Grand Major’s APAC Closed Qualifiers. The audio commentary that played over the video is at the center of this blowback, as the casters who originally commentated these matches were replaced by the game's fictional AI commentators, Scotty and June. While this video has since been removed from public viewing, remarks from casters in the community paint a grim picture of what they saw.
“After four cycles, open/closed [qualifiers], the time, effort, passion, and emotion myself, @TheeHyperactive, and @bluepanda_casts put in, we get replaced by two AI casters who even quote us. I get they are a part of the game, but yikes. Thanks @reachthefinals,” commentator Proto / Kai wrote in a viral post on Twitter/X.
After 4 cycles, open/closed quals, the time, effort, passion and emotion myself @TheeHyperactive and @bluepanda_casts put in. We get replaced by two Ai casters who even quote us :/ I get they are apart of the game but yikes. Thanks @reachthefinals https://t.co/oC8Zb5GrU0
Caster Bluepanda also spoke out on the situation, writing, “For nearly seven years I've been repeatedly told that my work is valued and appreciated, only to then have the same people saying those things turn around and either completely ghost me or tell me they're going in a different direction with talent and that my services aren't needed. GG.”
The ordeal soon caught fire within the general esports scene, with casters from various competitive gaming communities speaking out against Embark's decision to use AI as a replacement for the actual casters whose knowledge, charisma, and talent are being trained on without their knowledge or consent.
“Oh! Esports has AI casters now! Haha! I am appalled. These REAL casters deserve better, and stealing their quotes is disgusting. Y’know what’s worse? THE CASTING IS TERRIBLE. Everyone involved in making this should be embarrassed,” Marvel Rivals caster LemonKiwi wrote.
The Finals Gameplay Screenshots
“AI casters trained on the actual casters is devious, damn,” fighting game commentator Damascus tweeted. “Every day we keep moving towards the absolute slop era.”
Some players are pointing to a new feature for The Finals that was announced back in October called Dynamic Commentary. It uses the game’s pre-existing, fictional commentators Scotty and June, who are now able to refer to players by their screen names and even call out specific moments in individual matches based on the context of what’s happening in the game.
It's worth noting that the voices of Scotty and June were provided by human voice actors who were paid by Embark for their work. However, their lines are driven by a text-to-speech program and an artificial intelligence model that was trained on their voices, leading some players to argue that the writing for this AI esports commentary debacle has been on the wall for some time now.
I reached out to Embark Studios for comment on the situation. In its response, the company explained that it had chosen to use Scotty and June to introduce The Grand Major due to players' familiarity with the characters, but ultimately decided that this wasn't the right direction to take, given the hard work provided by the matches' original commentators and talent. The full statement can be read below:
"Yesterday, we released a recap video of THE FINALS APAC Closed Qualifier, narrated by Scotty and June, using familiar characters to introduce more players to THE FINALS esports ahead of The Grand Major. The video was a highlight recap, and our team selected clips from the broadcast, wrote an original script and produced new commentary for Scotty and June. However, leaving out the casters and talent who made that broadcast wasn’t the right call. We’ve taken the video down, and the AMER and EMEA recaps in the same format will no longer be released. We’re grateful to our talent for their candid feedback."
Oscar Lundberg, Competitive Experience and Community at Embark Studios and The Finals, published a statement on his personal Twitter/X account responding to the blowback, as well.
"Yesterday we released a recap of the APAC Closed Qualifier that left out the casters and talent who made that event. That was a mistake, and I’m sorry," he wrote. "We intended for Scotty and June to help bring more casual interest into THE FINALS esports ahead of TGM. That was the goal, but the work of our talent deserved to be included and highlighted, and it wasn’t. The video is down and won’t return in this form. The AMER and EMEA recaps planned in the same format won’t go out as planned either, and we’re rethinking all three."
I also spoke with two of the commentators who worked on The Finals' competitive circuit, both of whom were not chosen to commentate The Grand Major despite providing their talents for multiple tournaments leading up to the event. As Lundberg mentioned, this was just one of three highlight videos planned for each competing region using this type of AI audio commentary in place of the actual casters.
"Embark saw no issue with this until they received overwhelming global backlash and even then their response was essentially, 'Whoopsie, we didn't think people would mind,'" Bluepanda told me. "It says to me that they're not really sorry at all. I'm done with the game and esports as a whole at this stage, the effort we put in and the amount of bulls**t we have to deal with, especially in OCE, just isn't worth it anymore."
Proto, who commented all four cycles throughout the year, on top of working the open and closed qualifiers, echoed this sentiment and relayed how the situation was explained to him by Embark's organizers.
"It's definitely pretty tragic that they assumed that would be the right step forward," he said. "...They had an idea of the story that they wanted to tell for the teams and the qualifier. They looked through the VOD, found clips and moments that told that story, then wrote a script of what they roughly wanted Scotty and June to say. The script was handed off to an individual who writes the script, and then the line creation was done, and they didn't feed the VOD itself into the AI, but essentially they still ripped parts of the VOD of things that we said, which is why they copy things we said."
Proto went on to warn others in the industry that this debacle could be the proverbial canary in the coal mine for esports talent; much like the AI-generated menus we now see plastered on the exterior every restaurant, it's possible that one day, esports circuits no longer see the point in paying for flesh and blood talent when an AI is far cheaper.
"Opening that door is almost like Pandora's Box," Proto said. "As soon as it opens and people think that this is something that can be done, it creates problems for the talent who are pouring their heart and soul into these broadcasts. It just essentially takes away any kind of relevance from us in terms of, 'Why did we even bother?' I mean, they paid us to do this show. ...It was decent money. Why would you throw that away to dub us over with AI? It just didn't make any sense. And in terms of the longevity of the scene, I think this definitel opens up the ability for people now to experiment with [AI], if that's what they want to do, they can get rid of their talents."
As far as next steps are concerned, Proto says that all esports talent — be that casters, producers, broadcasters, camera operators, or even PAs — need to create a union to protect themselves from this exact type of mishap.
"I think industry wide, we definitely need to implement some kind of protection for commentary teams as well as production teams," he said. "There has to be some kind of something set up, whether it's a union, whether it's a global talent hiatus. We'll turn around and say, 'We're not doing this until people send us contracts that essentially ban the use of our voices in generative AI.' But this is why I include production, as well. If we've got people making streaming broadcasting packages or people running production on the back end of things, switching all the cameras, doing the observing, there are features that have auto-AI observe like in Counter-Strike, you can follow people from that third person perspective or even in the finals when people die, the camera will sort of just start flicking between people automatically. You got to protect those people's jobs."
But where Embark is concerned, Proto is calling for immediate and sweeping change. This includes widening the talent pool for major tournaments, providing a "more streamlined" version of next year's competitive events, and supporting local communities to keep the game's competitive scene alive.
"Everything has just been handled so poorly consistently to the point where even the talent announcement for the major, everybody wasn't happy. It's just been, and I say this brazenly, it's been a sh*t show. It's been a sh*t show," he said.
The Finals isn’t the only game from Embark that uses AI; Arc Raiders also utilizes artificial intelligence for voice lines that, similar to The Finals’ Dynamic Commentary, are able to call out specific items and locations.
In a November 2025 interview with PCGamesN, design director Virgil Watkins explained that Embark had “hire[d] and contract[ed] voice actors for it,” saying it was “part of their contract that we use [AI] for this purpose, and that allows us to do things like our ping system, where it's capable of saying every single item name, every single location name, and compass directions. That's how we can get that without needing to have someone come in every time we create a new item for the game."
Overall, it seems that most fans are in agreement that using AI for NPCs and player character dialogue is one thing, but replacing real-life commentators who poured hours into analysis with AI is another ball of wax, entirely.

item.title: The NBA's Miami Heat unveiled the special Vice City court they'll be playing on for one night only, tomorrow in a home game at the Kaseya Center against the Milwaukee Bucks.
item.description:
The NBA's Miami Heat unveiled the special Vice City court they'll be playing on for one night only, tomorrow in a home game at the Kaseya Center against the Milwaukee Bucks, which doubles as the first time that superstar Heat center Giannis Antetokounmpo will play against the team he'd spend his whole career with before being traded to Miami in the offseason.
Posting on the team's X page (see below), the court features the GTA 6 Roman-numeral "VI" logo along with "Vice CIty" at center court and "I love Vice City" along the baselines. All of it is in the now-familiar hot pink and blue color scheme that have been at the forefront of Grand Theft Auto 6's branding.
Introducing the Vice City hardwood 🏀See it for one night only, tomorrow vs Milwaukee. https://t.co/ZBpxND08hO
In tomorrow's game, the Heat will also be wearing one-off Vice City jerseys, though they sadly still say "Heat" on them rather than "Vice City." On the plus side, there is a whole bunch of Vice City merch available on the Miami Heat team store website.
After years of waiting, the release of GTA 6 is finally imminent (shout-out to all of the consoles "visiting" New Zealand in order to play a little earlier!). Make sure to update your preload if you haven't already so that you don't have to download anything before playing, and remember to stay in school (if applicable), as there might be a gift card in it for you. For those working, it looks like a whole bunch of you are taking PTO this week.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: GTA 6 fans are a bit surprised that the actor playing Jason wasn't nominated at The Game Awards.
item.description:
GTA 6 fans are a bit surprised that the actor playing Jason wasn't nominated at The Game Awards.
Earlier today, The Game Awards gave us our first indicator of how GTA 6 will be received. It's up for eight awards, including Game of the Year. It was a bit odd, as there are no reviews for the game at the moment, but the jury clearly deemed it worthwhile. The other notable thing to come out of the Game Awards nominations was that it confirmed the actress for Lucia: Manni L. Perez. Fans have speculated she was Lucia for years now, but now it's confirmed, as she was nominated for Best Performance.
However, the actor who plays the game's other protagonist was not nominated. Fans were taken aback, since the two are clearly a package deal in the game, and one has to imagine they elevate each other. However, the jury must not have felt strongly enough about Jason to give his actor the nomination. There's no rule against nominating multiple actors for a single project, either. Last year, three performers from Expedition 33 were all nominated in the same category, after all.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
Jason has been seen as a much more subtle and reserved character compared to Lucia. He's a bit quieter, isn't too flashy with his actions, and maybe lacks the fire in his character compared to someone like Lucia. One fan on Reddit noted that Jason didn't make a strong impression on them in any of the trailers: "Honestly, I'm not a fan of his VO," they said. "Jason doesn't sound good, at least in the footage we saw; he lacks diction. Most of the time, I can't understand what he's saying without subs."
However, another fan pushed back, noting that other great Rockstar actors have been snubbed in the past: "Benjamin Byron Davis wasn't nominated for his Dutch performance [in Red Dead Redemption 2]," they said. "Didn't take away one bit and [it's] arguably the best performance in the game."
It's certainly a valid point, especially since Rob Wiethoff also wasn't nominated for his role as John Marston in Red Dead Redemption 2, despite being a secondary protagonist. As of right now, we're not sure who is playing Jason, but it won't be long before we find out. GTA 6 will officially go live tomorrow morning in select regions, as the game becomes available in New Zealand. It'll be interesting to see which of the two protagonists fans end up gravitating toward more in the end, but it seems like Lucia may be a favorite based on her nomination.

item.title: Infinity Nikki players were baffled when Elon Musk’s mother, Maye Musk, appeared in a series of trailers announcing the game’s forthcoming 3.0 update on November 16.
item.description:
Infinity Nikki players were baffled when Elon Musk’s mother, Maye Musk, appeared in a series of trailers announcing the game’s forthcoming 3.0 update on November 16.
Yep, you read that correctly; Maye Musk appeared as a celebrity guest in commercials for the popular open-world dress-up game Infinity Nikki, which you can watch on the game’s official RedNote account (though you’ll need to make an account to view them). If you weren’t aware of this, you aren’t alone, as it seems that Maye’s advertisements weren’t exactly promoted on the game’s English-language social media profiles — and looking at comments on platforms like Twitter and Reddit, this strategy doesn’t come as a big surprise.
RedNote is a Chinese social media app that's most often compared to TikTok. Infinity Nikki is developed by PaperGames, a studio in mainland China, and boasts a strong fanbase in the country. So does Maye Musk, apparently, judging by the excited remarks on RedNote (a Chinese social app that’s often compared to TikTok).
Infinity Nikki Gameplay Screenshots
Maye Musk is something of a celebrity in China. Since at least 2023, the model and famous mum has appeared in all sorts of advertisements and campaigns in the country, representing brands that sell products like makeup, massage devices, and even down jackets, per a report from the New York Times. In that same report, Yang Hu, an expert on China’s beauty industry, explained her popularity: “[Her image] carries an element of successful parenting, attracting a significant number of mothers among her followers.”
These comments are echoed in the remarks that fans left on Billibilli’s live-streamed Infinity Nikki Version 3.0 First-Look Event. Automatic translations show that viewers were equal parts confused and delighted by her appearance as a host, with some writing, “Who the hell?” while others exclaimed, “Bestie, you’ve really made it big!” and, “You’re awesome!”
Given Elon Musk’s controversial nature in the West, comments on English social media sites were decidedly less positive.
“I can't believe what they've done here. I'm in shock. I was so excited to play version 3.0, but now I don't want to play anymore. What were they thinking? Can they genuinely recover from this?” one user wrote on Reddit.
“I’m out. That’ll teach me to sink money into a game. I literally justified the spending because I wanted to get a mental break away from these bulls**t people,” another said.
“I was thinking about trying this game. Now I certainly won't,” yet another admitted.
What do you hope the next big games industry trend will be?

item.title: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, who purchased MGM Studios in 2022 and assumed full control over the James Bond 007 franchise last year, shared details on the casting process and how the creative leads, including the director of the next 007 film Denis Villeneuve, ended up choosing The Batman and The Odyssey actor Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond.
item.description:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, who purchased MGM Studios in 2022 and assumed full control over the James Bond 007 franchise last year, shared details on the casting process and how the creative leads, including the director of the next 007 film Denis Villeneuve, ended up choosing The Batman and The Odyssey actor Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond.
Speaking at an event with media company Semafor, Bezos spoke for a couple of minutes on the Bond casting process (hat tip: Steve Jurvetson), saying he was "heavily involved" before detailing how it came down to Pattinson. "We ran a really tight process," he said. "We made the final decision on Friday. We down-selected to five finalists and then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists. And it was really interesting. Full costume, real sets, other actors with them. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists and then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all of the screen tests.
"All of the actors were extraordinarily talented. By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances. And it was immediately undebated. Denis, we all gravitated towards Rob."
Bezos and his team did question it for a bit, though. "Initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him just because he's already so famous," he explained. "We sort of thought maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown. But in the screening tests it was so obvious: he is James Bond."
Interestingly, after Bezos asked fans who they'd like to see as the next James Bond last year, Superman actor Henry Cavill won the popular vote. Instead, of course, an actor who has played DC's other ultra-famous superhero got the gig. Unfortunately, though, it stands to reason that Pattinson might not continue as Bruce Wayne and Batman after 2028's The Batman Part II.
It's been a heck of a year for Pattinson, certainly, between starring in The Odyssey, Primetime, The Drama, and next month's Dune: Part 3; filming The Batman Part II; and landing the role of Bond.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Gabe Newell, the co-founder and CEO of Valve, is being praised by fans after a yacht expert took a tour of his $500 million vessel and remarked on the “special” way he treats its crew, saying it rivals anything she’s “ever seen before.”
item.description:
Gabe Newell, the co-founder and CEO of Valve, is being praised by fans after a yacht expert took a tour of his $500 million superyacht and remarked on the “special” way he treats its crew, saying it rivals anything she’s “ever seen before.”
Gabe Newell is the proud owner of a $500 million superyacht named the Leviathan. It’s 111 meters long and boasts a few key features that were designed with its crew in mind. For example, it has a massive gaming center where guests, the owner, and staff can play video games together, as well as swanky VIP cabins that the crew can use if needed. They even have their own sleek, stylish rooms reserved just for employees, as well as swimming pools where they can receive their diving certifications. Gabe even commissioned a special glass panel engraved with the names of every person involved in the ship's design and construction.
Even the yacht’s flooring was intended to give the crew a break, ditching teak and wood in favor of a material that’s easier to clean. As told by Francesca Webster of the SuperYacht Times, it’s “a lot more functional for the crew, easy to clean, and gives them more time to do experiences with the owner and the guests on board.”
Photos From Gabe Newell's $500 Million Superyacht 'Leviathan'
Webster took a tour of the Leviathan for a video on the SuperYacht Times’ YouTube channel, where she remarked on how well Newell treats his staff and how unusual this is in the yachting business.
“Gabe actually opted to utilize this incredible space for the crew mess. He eats with the crew every day. They enjoy their meals together. It’s all about shared experience on board his boat. That’s something that we’ve really never seen before in our industry,” Webster said of the main deck saloon. She also revealed that Newell manages to keep staff for more than four and a half years — far more than the average superyacht staff retention of six to nine months.
The video quickly went viral, earning no shortage of praise from fans who couldn’t help but wonder how grim things in the yachting world must be if Newell is truly turning it on its head by treating his employees like equals.
“‘He has a different perspective on interacting with the people on board’ — SuperYacht enjoyer describing someone who doesn’t hate people,” one commenter joked on YouTube.
“This entire video is, ‘It astonishes me that Gabe actually cares about his crew and treats them as people. It’s so rare to see an owner who respects humans around them,’” another said.
“The fact this is such an outrageous world- first that the crew is seen as actual people tells you all you need to know,” another wrote.
This isn't the only big purchase from Newell to make headlines; earlier this year, Newell purchased a $70.8 million mansion in Manalapan, Florida that comes with a dock and boat lift for his yacht, an in-ground pool, an eight-car garage, and even an underground tunnel that leads out to an adjoining beach.
This is one of the more recent insights we’ve gotten into the life of Gabe Newell after a Counter-Strike’s co-creator revealed that Newell got so obsessed with Mongolian Throat singing at one point that employees would close their office doors to muffle the sound of him practicing in Valve’s corporate headquarters.
Image Credits: SuperYacht Times, YouTube

Following announcements from Nintendo and PlayStation, Xbox has officially revealed the details of its Black Friday sale.
Deals go live on November 19 — this Friday — at 9am PST. The big headliner is up to 80% digital Xbox and PC games, with additional discounts on Xbox accessories, including custom engraved controllers. What there’s no mention of, though? Consoles.
Xbox Black Friday Sale 2026
Xbox was kind enough to offer a sneak peek of the over 2,000 games that will go on sale. These are digital-only deals, but we’re keeping an eye out for physical game deals at Amazon and Best Buy.
Fresh discounts on 2026 releases include 30% off Gears of War: E-Day, 25% off Forza Horizon 6, and for the sports-inclined, 55% off NBA 2K27 and 50% off Madden NFL 27. Final Fantasy VII Remake Integrate, Crimson Desert, The Blood of Dawnwalker, and Halo: Campaign Evolved will also go on sale.
A selection of Xbox controller discounts are already available through the Xbox direct store, and it’s unclear whether those prices will be dropping any further. In addition to the base controller discounts, Xbox is offering up to 15% off custom controllers from the Xbox Design Lab, complete with free engravings.
Finally, Xbox is collaborating with Samsung on its Black Friday bundle. Nope, it doesn’t include any games or consoles. Instead, the bundle feels like a lingering remnant of the controversial "Everything Is an Xbox" campaign, which was technically retired soon after Asha Sharma was named CEO. Nonetheless, for Black Friday 2026, eligible Samsung TVs will come with Xbox’s new Nano controller and two months of Game Pass Ultimate.
So, what’s going on with the consoles? Well, it’s not just Xbox. We already knew that PlayStation is skipping out on the console deals this year, just as both systems are getting the biggest game launch of all time. (GTA 6, in case that wasn’t clear).
Unfortunately, we’re in the thick of RAMageddon, an ongoing memory shortage that has contributed to supply issues and price hikes across the console and tech space. Even worse, launches like GTA 6 have increased console demand despite higher prices, giving Xbox and PlayStation little reason to try and squeak out a discount.
If you're desperate for any console, I’d check out the Switch 2, the only option getting a Black Friday deal. If you're specifically looking to play GTA, your best bet is keeping an eye out for solid refurbished deals.

item.title: IGN has conducted a poll on if our readers would be taking time off to play GTA 6, and nearly half of them said yes.
item.description:
IGN has conducted a poll on if our readers would be taking time off to play GTA 6, and nearly half of them said yes.
We are officially less than a week away from the release of GTA 6, which means fans are preparing their launch plans as we speak. Economists have estimated that the U.S. economy will incur a $1 billion loss in productivity when the game launches on Thursday due to people calling out sick. We asked IGN readers if they will be part of that drop in productivity, and it seems like a significant amount of them will be.
The poll had three options, two of which allowed fans to choose whether or not they'd be using PTO or calling in sick on the day of release. The third choice were for users who plan to go into work on November 19. At the time of writing, over 39,000 users have voted, and 46.5% of them stated that they would be taking the day off to play GTA 6 using either PTO or by calling in sick at launch, while 53.3% stated that they wouldn't be taking time off.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
The full break down for each poll option is as follows:
Are IGN Readers Taking Time Off to Play GTA 6?
Yes, I am requesting/have already requested PTO - 38.3%
Yes, but I am calling sick on the day of release - 8.2%
GTA 6 is expected to have one of the largest entertainment launches of all time and will likely shatter GTA 5's records. Rockstar set new records in 2013 for having the fastest entertainment product to hit $1 billion, with $815 million of that coming in the first day. Given GTA 6 will actually cost more than GTA 5 ($80 for the standard version, $100 for the ultimate edition), it wouldn't be surprising if Rockstar blows way past that. The game has also managed to earn some early praise, as GTA 6 is nominated for eight awards at The Game Awards, including the highly sought-after Game of the Year trophy.
To make sure fans are aware of the cultural juggernaut's looming release, Rockstar has been turning Miami into Vice City in real life. The city is currently plastered with in-universe ads for GTA brands, with GTA-branded cars driving all over the place, a Vice City blimp flying over it, and the Miami Heat's arena has even been decked out with Vice City signage. Rockstar also paid $975,000 to install a neon pink sign that reads "Welcome to Vice City." Tomorrow, Rockstar will sponsor a regular season Miami Heat game and turn the team into the Vice City Heat with new jerseys and a never-before-seen court.
The game is less than 24 hours from beginning its regional roll out, starting with New Zealand. With all of that said, if you're one of the people skipping work or school play, make sure you pre-load the game so you don't waste a second of your precious time off downloading the game. And while you wait, be sure to check out our interviews with various content creators to see how they're preparing for this gargantuan launch, as well as community members who are preparing to say goodbye to GTA 5.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Florence Pugh has thrown her hat in the ring in the hopes of becoming the next Bond villain after news of Robert Pattinson’s casting took over social media yesterday.
item.description:
Florence Pugh has thrown her hat in the ring in the hopes of becoming the next Bond villain after news of Robert Pattinson’s casting took over social media yesterday.
Robert Pattinson is your new James Bond, as revealed in an official video clip on November 16 that subsequently went viral. His casting has sparked no end of debate among fans, with some welcoming him into the fold with open arms, while others are arguing that they’d much prefer the likes of Henry Cavill, instead (though it seems Cavill wasn’t in the final list of actors who tested for the role).
Now that we have our new Bond, fans are going wild, sharing their personal picks for a villain to play opposite him — and even some A-list actors are vying for the part. Florence Pugh is one such actor, who admitted that she’d immediately texted director Denis Villeneuve out of interest in the part.
The Next James Bonds Who Never Played 007
"Congratulations on finding your Bond, nice catch. Any villains the size of a 5ft 4in female?" she said at Elle’s Women in Hollywood event, recounting the message she’d sent him.
Pugh isn’t the only one gunning to be a Bond villain. Brad Pitt also expressed interest in the idea, telling Extra TV when approached with the topic, "You know what, I'd like to do that. I mean, my man Javier [Bardem] did it so well. It's tall shoes, but I'd take that on, yeah."
Pitt also had some kind words for Pattinson after learning of his casting, saying, “Is that right? You know what, I love this idea. I love what he's been doing. I love his choices, I think he's the real deal. That's great, good call."
Even former Bond actor George Lazenby weighed in on the news, giving Pattinson some sage advice as someone who has already played the part and experienced all the opinions that came with it.
“I hear they've announced the new James Bond,” Lazenby wrote in a post shared on social media. “Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let's see if you'll have [a] ‘This never happened to the other fella!’ moment. All the best, mate, George xx.”
Pattinson reportedly competed with Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, and Nicholas Hoult for Bond, and was even given a far more lucrative deal for less films than other talent in the running. He auditioned for the role while filming for The Batman Part II was on pause — a project that now sits in limbo thanks to his latest gig.
While we likely won’t be seeing anything from Pattinson’s Bond for some time, fans can whet their appetites with Dune: Part Three, which comes to theaters this December.
Image Credits: Brianna Bryson/FilmMagic
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Microsoft's 25th anniversary translucent green Xbox Series X consoles began arriving this week for those who were able to secure one, and unfortunately a number of them are running into an all-too-common theme: a damaged box. Granted, the cardboard box on the outside is far less important than the plastic box on the inside, but with a limited-edition collectible like this – Microsoft produced just 25,000 of these X25 units – it's left some fans frustrated and disappointed.
item.description:
Microsoft's 25th anniversary translucent green Xbox Series X consoles began arriving this week for those who were able to secure one, and unfortunately a number of them are running into an all-too-common theme: a damaged box. Granted, the cardboard box on the outside is far less important than the plastic box on the inside, but with a limited-edition collectible like this – Microsoft produced just 25,000 of these X25 units – it's left some fans frustrated and disappointed.
Longtime IGN reader Matt Fizell reached out to me directly to first flag this issue to IGN. As you can see in the photos below, his console arrived with a not-insignificant tear to the box. Matt says his order came from the Microsoft Store, which apparently didn't include any packing peanuts or other protection in the shipping box. Further exploration of this revealed other posts on X and Facebook about this, as well as an entire Reddit thread that included many others suffering from the same shipping damage. Microsoft had not responded to IGN's request for comment by the time of publication.
The 25th anniversary Xbox Series X X25 console was announced during this year's Xbox Showcase, and unsurprisingly sold out in seconds despite a retail price of $899. The translucent green controller was sold separately for those who didn't want or couldn't afford the console, but as of this writing it appears to be sold out everywhere as well. Xbox did just announce its Black Friday deals, though, if you weren't able to get your hands on the X25 console or controller.
Xbox's 25th year has been an eventful one, to say the least. Longtime Xbox boss Phil Spencer retired and was replaced by Asha Sharma, who has wasted no time in making big moves, such as slashing the price of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, getting rid of the "This is an Xbox" marketing campaign, taking Halo away from Halo Studios and handing it to Activision, and signing Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor Physint when Sony dropped it, among other things. Unfortunately she's also laid off thousands of people.
I wrote about my biggest memories of covering Xbox throughout its wild first quarter-century in the console business last weekend to mark the official 25th anniversary on November 15.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Want a free $5 discount at Amazon? You can get one now by texting Alexa to shop.
item.description:
The tech world is changing fast, friends. Amazon’s latest bid to get people to shop through its Alexa AI assistant is to give away free cash. Right now, if you use Alexa’s new “shop by text” ability, you can get $5 off your first order. All you have to do is text the digital assistant what you want to buy, and you’ll get the discount. You can do it here.
On that page, make sure you’re signed into your Amazon account and click the “Text Alexa” button. A box will pop up to verify the phone number associated with your account. Click “Agree and text,” and you’ll receive a text message from Alexa Shopping. Reply to that text to search for whatever ou want to buy, and you'll get an instant $5 discount.
The deal only works on items sold by Amazon and third-party sellers on the site. You can’t use it on gift cards, subscriptions, or digital content. And the promo may end at any time, so you’ll probably want to do it sooner rather than later if you’re interested in saving $5.
Texting with Alexa is just like interacting with the AI over an Echo device or using the app. You can chat with the assistant to find the item you’re looking to purchase. You can send a photo of an item to have Alexa identify it and make your purchase that way. If you need more info about this whole “texting Alexa” thing, you can probably find it on this page, which features an FAQ and has all the information about what qualifies and doesn’t for the $5 discount on your first order.
Outside of gaming, what are you actually buying during Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales?

item.title: Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games is laying off around 60 people, which amounts to approximately one third of its workforce, according to a Bloomberg report. The studio head of the Maryland-based development studio is also departing.
item.description:
Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games is laying off around 60 people, which amounts to approximately one third of its workforce, according to a Bloomberg report. The studio head of the Maryland-based development studio is also departing.
2K, the publishing arm that handles Firaxis, BioShock games, the Mafia series, and various sports titles under Take-Two, gave Bloomberg a comment on the layoffs.
“Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength — designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years,” said a 2K spokesperson.
Civilization 7 Gameplay Screenshots
“As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”
The 4X strategy game series has been one of the quiet giants under the 2K label, but the most recent entry, Civilization 7, divided players. Reviews for the game on Steam are mixed, with players complaining about radical structural changes to long-standing franchise traditions, a lack of polish, and predatory implementation of monetization.
According to the report, Firaxis is also working on a new game in its turn-based alien invasion series, XCOM. However, the team has been facing development struggles and recently missed a key development milestone.
Bloomberg’s anonymous sources claim that development of the new XCOM will continue, but will likely face some kind of shakeup following the cuts to staffing.
Firaxis also laid off an unannounced number of developers last year, following the launch of Civilization 7, despite 2K claiming sales of the game were “consistent with expectations.”
The studio’s previous major launch, Marvel’s Midnight Suns, performed poorly. At the time, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick told Bloomberg that "it's possible the release window wasn't perfect" but that he thinks it could keep selling over a long period of time.
What do you think of Civilization 7 now compared to the launch version?

item.title: The 2026 Game Award nominations have finally been revealed.
item.description:
The 2026 Game Award nominations have finally been revealed. This is arguably one of the biggest years in gaming, as it has featured some of the hottest, most anticipated games out there. We got the long-awaited return of Leon Kennedy in Resident Evil Requiem, the release of 007 First Light, which fans had been waiting for since 2020, and, of course, the launch of GTA 6.
With the year coming to an end, The Game Awards has revealed the nominees for 2026 ahead of the ceremony on December 10. As you might have predicted, GTA 6 swept with eight nominations, including the coveted Game of the Year. Yes, we really got GTA 6 nominated for Game of the Year before GTA 6. There's it's competing with 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for the main award.
The Game Awards 2026 nominations also confirms, finally, the actor who plays Lucia in GTA 6. Manni L. Perez, who many fans had suspected played Lucia in Rockstar's game, is nominated in the Best Performance category. The actor who plays fellow GTA 6 protagonist Jason doesn't make the cut.
GTA 6 Dynamic Weather Screenshots
Nintendo is The Game Awards’ most nominated publisher in 2026 with 12 nominations across its combined portfolio, followed by Capcom with 11 nominations, and Annapurna Interactive and PlayStation with nine nominations each. item.title: On the eve of launching GTA 6, we finally now know who portrays main character Lucia Caminos.
item.description:
On the eve of launching GTA 6, we finally now know who portrays main character Lucia Caminos.
Today's big reveal came via a blink-and-you'll miss it moment during The Game Awards' nominations livestream, where Manni L. Perez was nominated for her role in GTA 6. Unfortunately, we still don't know who is playing her co-star Jason Duval, as his actor did not get nominated. Ouch.
The announcement comes after months of speculation around who is bringing Grand Theft Auto's first ever playable couple to life, and some very careful social media livestreams from the long-rumored Lucia actress where Perez dodged constant comments about her part in perhaps the most anticipated video game of all time.
Somewhat incredibly, Rockstar is still to officially announce GTA 6's voice cast — and the only reason we're getting the confirmation of Perez today is because of her award nomination.
Perez is an actress with a smattering of credits to her acting resume, including TV guest roles in Jessica Jones, Chicago P.D. and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. While she hasn't been up to much else over the past few years, it's perhaps easy to now know why — it's likely she has been kept very busy working GTA 6 instead.
Fun fact: this won't actually be Perez's first GTA role. In GTA 5, Perez portrays the background character of "Clubber #2," while in GTA Online she voices a blackjack dealer.
In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023
Last month, the actors behind GTA 5's Franklin, Michael, and Trevor shared their advice for GTA 6's cast in a bid to ready them for the kind of fame few video game actors achieve.
GTA 6 is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, and some companies have even given staff bonus time off to play it. We've got plenty more on GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 launch, including details on the New Zealand trick people are using to play early, Gangland Tales From the Frontline of Rockstar's Real-Life Grand Theft Auto Research, and How Gaming's Top Content Creators Are Preparing for GTA 6's Launch and Beyond.

item.title: Former Nvidia boss Jensen Huang has said he is ready to return to the company he co-founded, after he resigned amid a scandal involving infidelity and alleged espionage.
item.description:
Former Nvidia boss Jensen Huang has said he is ready to return to the company he co-founded, after he resigned amid a scandal involving infidelity and alleged espionage.
In a social media post, Huang issued a statement apologizing for the problems he'd caused both Nvidia and his family, and insisted he would be willing to return as CEO if Nvidia's Board of Directors decided it was in the best interest in the company.
Huang's statement comes after it was reported that he will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select Committees on December 1. "The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal,” Reps. Brian Mast, R-Fla., John Moolenaar, R-Mich., and Rick Crawford, R-Ark., the chairs of the Foreign Affairs, China Select and Intelligence Committees, said in a statement reported by CNBC.
Here is Huang's statement in full:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.
I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.
Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.
Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

item.title: Sony has fought off a legal challenge over the pricing of PlayStation games that argued the company charged "excessive and unfair prices."
item.description:
Sony has fought off a legal challenge over the pricing of PlayStation games that argued the company charged "excessive and unfair prices."
The class action lawsuit, filed in the U.K. earlier this year by consumer rights campaigner Alex Neil, claimed that PlayStation had overcharged customers due to its 30% cut of all digital games and add-ons — essentially, anything sold via the PlayStation Store.
The legal action suggested that Sony's pricing was unfair and its profit margins were excessive. Additionally, it was claimed that PlayStation held a "near monopoly" on video games — in particular, that it forced users to buy from its own digital store rather than offering a range of alternatives.
The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time
As reported by The Game Business, London's Competition Appeal Tribunal has now tossed out the lawsuit, on the grounds that PlayStation had not been proven to have broken anti-competition laws.
If successful, the court case would have seen an estimated 12.2 million PlayStation owners in the U.K. compensated for a decade of purchases, amounting to around $215 per person.
In more detail, the new ruling noted that video game fans had a choice of where to play video games — on rival consoles, PC and elsewhere — and that physical games were also currently an option. (It'll be interesting to see how that changes in future.)
Because of this, PlayStation was under no obligation to invite third-party stores onto its platform, the tribunal decided, as Sony was just one player in a larger market. Finally, it was agreed that Sony's decision to sell consoles relatively cheaply (compared to their actual cost) indicated that the company was not trying to fleece customers unfairly, even if prices were rising.
Of course, Sony's 30% cut of digital purchases is standard across the industry, with Nintendo, Microsoft and Steam believed to operate similarly. And while PlayStation console prices have risen, the same could be said for all other console manufacturers too, due to factors largely beyond their control.
That said, PlayStation could hardly be argued to be struggling financially right now. Sony announced that PS5 had passed the 100 million consoles sold milestone only last week, and that's before the impending arrival of GTA 6.

item.title: McDonald's is launching a massive Home Alone collaboration for the holiday season, and Macaulay Culkin has reprised his role as Kevin to celebrate.
item.description:
McDonald's is launching a massive Home Alone collaboration for the holiday season.
The promotion, available across U.S. locations on December 1, comes with Home Alone variants for some of the fast-food chain's most popular meals. We’re talking Quarter Pounders, Nuggets, and, of course, the Big Mac.
Each meal comes with one pair of collectible socks, with four total pairs available across the promotion. The limited-time offer also introduces several new pizza-flavored McDonald’s menu items inspired by Kevin’s hijinks.
Macaulay Culkin reprised his role as the mischievous Kevin to promote the collaboration. A new commercial features grown-up Kevin having a blast in an emptied out McDonald’s restaurant — and showing off his new socks.
"What I love about this collaboration is that the 'Home Alone Meal' captures something bigger than just one character," said Culkin in a statement. "It's about the playful spirit that resonates with people across generations."
To achieve that playful spirit, the Home Alone Meal swaps regular McDonald's fries for the new Pizza McShaker flavor, which comes with a Little Nero’s seasoning packet. Otherwise, most of the meals are pretty similar to the standard versions, just with some socks thrown in.
The four pairs of collectible socks each feature a specific character: Kevin himself, and some McDonald's classics — Grimace, the Hamburglar, and Birdie the Early Bird. They’re pretty much your standard holiday socks, detailed with the classic Golden Arches logo and a small image of the McCallister's house.
McDonald's Home Alone Meal - Images
Two new standalone items will also be available for a limited time: the Mini Pizza Sharebox and the Everything Sundae McFlurry. The Little Nero's pizza box comes with four crispy cheese and tomato pizza pies, while the McFlurry is packed with Oreos, crushed Smarties, and a chocolate sauce. The pizza obviously references Kevin’s big order in Home Alone, while the McFlurry references Kevin’s gargantuan sundae in Home Alone 2. Yep, we’re getting into sequel territory.
Of course, this wouldn’t be a real fast-food collab without a funky new sauce. The pizza theme continues with 'Lovely Cheese Pizza Dipping Sauce,' a creamy blend of parmesan cheese, tomato flavor, and garden herbs.
The Home Alone Meal launches on December 1 for as long as supplies last. Disney+ trials are being added to McDonald’s Rewards for in-app purchases, giving you a chance to watch the movie while you enjoy your pizza fries. McDonald’s is also currently offering the Pokémon Happy Meal, which will likely run concurrently with the Home Alone collab.
What would you order from the Home Alone meal?

item.title: Ahead of GTA 6's release, GTA 5 fans are reflecting on their 13 years of history with the beloved open-world crime game.
item.description:
Today, gamers around the world are saying their goodbyes to GTA 5, a game that has been with them for as long as 13 years. Its initial release was a massive moment for many; not only was it yet another exciting new, ambitious entry into one of gaming’s most beloved franchises, but it would also be a catalyst for so much more for millions of people.
For me, I was just 12 years old. It was an inappropriate age to be playing such a game, but after following the pre-release hype for months and playing it myself, it had a massive impact on me. It set me on the path that I am on today and inspired me to pursue a career in games media, partially so I could cover GTA 6 when it came out.
And now, we’re here. I have spent literally half of my life chasing this moment. It was a journey of all kinds of ups and downs, but I am hardly alone in that journey. Millions of GTA 5 fans have forged friendships, lost loved ones, and experienced life-altering changes during the game's undeterred longevity.
Every Celebrity in GTA 5 and GTA Online
Take GTA YouTuber TGG as an example. He has 2.32 million subscribers, and his story largely traces back to GTA 5. Although he had dabbled in other GTA games prior to this, 5 was the game that really hooked him. In 9th grade, his dad bought him the game and essentially unlocked a whole new world for him. The sandbox elements within GTA Online were immediately captivating for a young teenager, leading to memories he still holds dearly to this day.
“It was freedom,” he said in reference to what made GTA Online special in its earliest days. “No other game would just drop people in an open world and say, 'Do whatever the f**k you want.'"
But it wasn’t just about blowing stuff up or mowing down NPCs for him. When things weren’t going well at home or in his personal life, GTA Online offered an escape, but one that wasn’t overly-isolating. It was like a virtual third space where he could hang out with people from school and find common ground, allowing him to make new friends with kids he may not have otherwise been able to connect with.
“I think one of the reasons those memories are so special to me was because it helped [me make friends]. Racing with people from school, you end up with a full lobby of 16 people. Maybe you only know three or four of them very well, but that's 10 new people from your school that you're racing with that you can build friendships with. And being able to talk about whatever happened in a race or whatever happened in a mission that you were grinding out together, and having an icebreaker with people at school the next day really helped. I don't want to say [it] helped [me] get through school necessarily, but [it] helped expand my circle.
"And to me, as someone who was always a more quiet kid and wasn't the most popular kid in school, those [moments] were very important to me. And I think looking at it a bit deeper, that's probably the reason that those memories are more special to me because they helped me expand my circle at school when it was probably pretty small.”
TGG eventually spun his love and encyclopedic knowledge of GTA Online into a career. He launched a YouTube channel while he was still in school and took inspiration from another creator known as TmarTn for the kinds of videos he wanted to make. After making over a thousand videos, TGG has become a leading source for GTA news, partially because he is the one breaking it himself. He was invited to Rockstar North earlier this year and given the opportunity to preview the game, allowing him to bring a bunch of exclusive info back to his viewers. It’s a surreal moment.
TmarTn, whose real name is Trevor Martin, is still making GTA videos. He has over 5.69 million subscribers on his most active channel and has made countless videos about the franchise. GTA 6’s launch is a sort of full circle moment for him, as his journey with the franchise largely began with the original Vice City.
“The first one I had was Vice City on PS2. So it's kind of cool because it's this full moment. I was a little kid playing this, worried about the loading screens that were popping up and things like that, trying to hide it from my mom. And now I'm back in Vice City and I'm a grown mid-thirties man and I'm still... It's kind of the same vibe. You know what I mean? It's still just as exciting.”
TGG and TmarTn aren’t the only ones whose love for GTA 5 led to fruitful careers. 31-year-old Adam Butterworth was a fan of the game since day one and it became a staple of his life. Every December, Rockstar adds snow to GTA Online and a bunch of holiday festivities, and experiencing this became a holiday tradition for Butterworth.
“Every Christmas Day me and a few mates would load the game [up], [drive] to the parking lot in the city center, go to the roof, and just chat while trying to push each other off the roof or break the car. It was stupid but it was a good time and as we got older and game time became harder to get among us it became something we would be excited for on Christmas… besides the ungodly amount of food and presents.”
Eventually, his love for GTA 5 turned into something more: a job at Rockstar Games. After bearing the elements in a historic UK snowstorm to attend a job interview, Butterworth scored a gig working in the developer’s QA department. In the lead-up to his first day at the company, he immersed himself even further into GTA 5’s world.
“While waiting for my start date, every day I would do the drive around the map and just think that in a few weeks I would get to work with the team that made this game, a game that meant so much to me.”
A Rockstar community member named Josh, AKA Vinewood Motors, has also managed to turn GTA Online into something more than just a game. After building a sizable social media presence sharing content, Josh began to use his following for good. He has raised over $40,000 for charity as part of a series of GTA-centric Gameblast streams over the years. The annual charity streams have become so significant that Rockstar Games has also supported them.
Still, some people don’t have grand ambitions for GTA Online. Some of them just want somewhere they can spend their time and be social. A 22-year-old GTA 5 fan named Harry told me that he spent over 4,300 hours in the game over the last decade. Not unlike others, it has become a source of core memories with his friends.
“Over the last 11 years, I’ve had so many fond memories doing heists, races, adversary modes, and just running around in freemode. I still remember the rush my friends and I felt after finally completing the Doomsday Heist finale for the first time, after many attempts and a lot of arguing.”
All of those memories have culminated in a special event that players are dubbing “The Last Ride.” This isn’t an official in-game event from Rockstar, it’s one created by the community. Players will drive around San Andreas by looping around its highway before ending up at the airport. They then plan to board a jet and fly off into the east toward Vice City while the sun sets behind them. It’s a way to say goodbye to a place they’ve called home for years.
“My plan for GTA 6 launch night is to drive around Los Santos with my friends and talk about some of our favourite memories,” said Harry. “We’re gonna take our favourite cars, say goodbye to landmarks like the casino, our yachts, apartments, and nightclubs. Then, as soon as the clock strikes midnight, we’re opening GTA 6.”
“I’ll say goodbye to a game that has seen me go from university, to Rockstar, to Remedy [Entertainment], to being a home owner, getting married and becoming a dad,” said Butterworth. “13 years of enjoyment and memories.”
Like many others I spoke to for this story, 22-year-old Brian Berkman got GTA fever at a young age and had to wear down his mom so she’d buy the game for him. Now, as he prepares to leave GTA 5 behind, he’s driving through Los Santos like he’s leaving his hometown behind.
“It sounds a little corny on paper but this is the one singular video game that has stuck around for what feels like my entire life; some people have that with Minecraft but I was admittedly never as big a Minecraft guy as others,” said Berkman. “It’s always been GTA 5 for me even before I owned the game myself, sometimes it feels like I know the in-game map better than my own real-life neighborhood sometimes.
“Even when I’d have nothing to do in the game itself I’d find myself driving around Los Santos blasting Non-Stop-Pop FM feeling like I had my own home away from home, while simultaneously in the comfort of my own home. Everytime I’d think this game was getting too old, Mike Posner 'Cooler Than Me' would come on and all of that would wash away, and I’d feel like I was playing the coolest game in the world. Hearing that come on the radio one last time will have me unreasonably emotional on November 18.”
This will also be a moment for some fans to honor those who didn’t make it to GTA 6. 28-year-old Tobias Johnson plans to use this send off to GTA Online as a way to remember his friend, Noah, who passed away almost a decade ago.
“[This] will be a chance to relive the memories I was able to have with my friends, especially Noah, who I lost at 19 years old in 2017,” said Johnson. “I think about him every day and some of the best memories I have of him are from playing whatever random game mode or race on GTA Online together. The last ride will be symbolic for me as this is kinda just taking that next step in life.
“I’m almost 30 now and while I can always go back to GTA 5, this will be a nice little bit of closure on that time of my life and it will be incredibly cathartic to drive around Los Santos and really soak in those memories of Noah and I one last time.”
Are You Taking Time Off For GTA 6's Release?

item.title: Carina Conti plays the female version of Jun Aslan in the upcoming sci-fi RPG Exodus alongside Stephen Oyoung as male Jun.
item.description:
We've seen the upcoming spacefaring sci-fi RPG Exodus from many angles already and even had an extensive hands-on preview where I got to play through an entire mission. Everything from its blend of shooter and RPG combat to the kinds of choices you'll make at pivotal moments as lead protagonist Jun Aslan. But two major things that've been kept under wraps until now were the character model and voice of female Jun – like Mass Effect, players can choose to play as a male or female version of the main character. Through a new story trailer, we finally saw and heard female Jun in action for the first time who is being voiced by actor Carina Conti.
Conti has appeared in shows such as Good Trouble on Hulu and Winning Time on HBO, as well as the Sundance award-winning comedy-drama Junk (previously titled Little Death). She also had a leading role in Mafia: The Old Country as the character Isabella Torrisi, and now she'll be our scrappy salvager turned space traveler Jun Aslan in Exodus.
Male Jun is being portrayed by actor Stephen Oyoung who has made appearances in movies such as Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. And he has video game credits as Mister Negative in Marvel's Spider-Man and Spider-Man 2 and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. We've been able to hear his version of Jun throughout all previous content in Exodus, and more recently, developer Archetype Entertainment tweaked the face model of male Jun based on audience feedback.
As previously stated in our preview and interview with Archetype, regardless of which version of Jun players choose, the dialogue, story, and romance options remain the same even if the performances will be different. In a conversation with both Conti and Oyoung, they jokingly mentioned that recording romance scenes were both traumatic and hilarious, but they also spoke to embodying Jun as a character.
"I love her [female Jun], I'm a little bit obsessed with her! She embodies qualities that I really envision for my future self," Conti said. "Getting to practice those [qualities] within her over the course of six months was such a luxury. It was like, what if you already got to play this version of yourself where you are powerful, confident, and courageous, and a leader of men where you really have your ducks in a row."
Exodus is set to launch on April 7, 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. Be sure to check out my last hands-on preview with Exodus covering the mission on the ship colony of Khonsu where we saved a species of intelligent frogs from control from an evil faction and made a game-changing decision about their fate. You can also read my interview with narrative director Drew Karphysyn (known for writing Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and Mass Effect) where he explained choice and consequence in Exodus and how his time at BioWare shaped his upcoming work. Speaking of Mass Effect, I also interviewed Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, the voices of Commander Shepard, to talk about the closure of BioWare and what Mass Effect meant to them.
Michael is reviews editor at IGN and regularly contributes with previews, interviews, live events coverage, and news all in written and video form. He's usually entrusted with covering long RPGs and tech products, but he's got range when it comes to games. You'll also catch him at conventions and hosting video content, including IGN's weekly podcast Unlocked.
